title: Zero-Point Security CRTO
summary: The Certified Red Team Operator (CRTO) from Zero-Point Security is a practical red team certification built around adversary simulation against a Windows Active Directory environment using Cobalt Strike and supporting tools. Active Directory is the Microsoft service that most companies use to manage users, computers and permissions, so it is the prize in most real intrusions. This certification sits at an advanced level and assumes you are already comfortable with Windows, command line work and basic penetration testing; it is not a first offensive certificate. The exam is entirely practical. You work through a live lab over a 48 hour window that you may pause and spread across several days, and you pass by capturing six of eight flags, which proves to an employer that you can perform reconnaissance, escalate privileges, move laterally and reach domain level access under your own direction. It leads to roles such as red team operator, adversary simulation specialist, senior penetration tester and offensive security consultant. Zero-Point Security publishes the course as a sequence of topics rather than as weighted exam domains, so the chapters below follow that published order and no percentages are claimed. This is an independent study guide and is not official Zero-Point Security material; confirm the current exam details with the vendor before you book.

beginner.definition: The Certified Red Team Operator is an advanced certificate from Zero-Point Security. A red team is a group that attacks its own company on purpose. It does this with permission, to test how well the defenders cope. This certification checks that you can carry out that kind of attack in a Windows network.
beginner.whyItMatters: Defenders learn most from a real attack. Companies hire people who can copy the way criminals work. This certificate proves that you can do that against the system most businesses depend on. It is respected because the exam is practical and you cannot pass it by memorising facts. That makes it a strong credential for senior offensive roles. It also helps in a security operations centre.
howItWorks: Build your base first. Learn Windows, Active Directory and the command line before you start.
Study the published course topics in order so you understand how an intrusion usually unfolds.
Set up a small practice domain with a few machines and a domain controller you own.
Practise running a command and control framework and keeping your access hidden from defenders.
Rehearse the full chain from first access to domain level control. Keep going until you can do it without notes.
The exam gives you a lab for 48 hours. Practise working in long sessions and taking notes as you go.
beginner.example: Think of a large office where every door opens with the same staff badge. An attacker who copies one badge can walk almost anywhere. A red team operator does the same in a network. You get one ordinary account. You find where its password is stored and reuse it on another machine. You keep climbing until you hold the keys to the whole building. The CRTO exam asks you to climb that ladder inside the time allowed.
takeaways: This is not a beginner certificate, so gain real Windows and testing experience first.
The exam is practical and time limited, so practise complete attack chains rather than single tricks.
Learn to stay quiet. Detection is part of the test, not an accident.

objectives: Plan a red team engagement and explain the rules that keep it legal and safe
Build and operate command and control infrastructure that survives defenders
Reconnoiter a Windows Active Directory environment from inside and outside
Escalate privileges on a host and steal credentials for reuse
Move laterally through a network and reach domain level control
Evade common endpoint protections and report the operation clearly

chapters.title: Red team concepts, engagement planning and reporting
objectives: Explain how red teaming differs from a standard penetration test
Agree scope, rules of engagement and safety limits with the client
Design a campaign that copies realistic attacker behaviour
Keep operational notes that support the final report
Write a report that shows what an attacker achieved and what should change

chapters.title: Command and control with Cobalt Strike
objectives: Stand up a command and control listener and explain how it works
Configure a payload that fits the target environment
Adapt beacon settings to control how often the implant calls home
Manage multiple compromised hosts from one console
Explain why command and control design decides whether you are detected

chapters.title: Host reconnaissance and privilege escalation
objectives: Reconnoiter a compromised host for users, groups, software and permissions
Find misconfigurations that allow a normal user to gain more rights
Escalate privileges on a Windows host and confirm the new level of access
Collect local administrator credentials and explain how they are reused
Decide which host is worth the next step and why

chapters.title: Credential theft and password cracking
objectives: Extract credential material from a Windows host in a controlled way
Explain how Windows stores and protects passwords and hashes
Crack captured hashes and choose the right cracking approach for each case
Move from a stolen credential to a usable session
Recognise which credential findings matter most to the client

chapters.title: Lateral movement and pivoting
objectives: Move from one host to another using valid accounts and remote services
Pivot through a compromised host to reach a network you cannot see directly
Set up and use a proxy to route tooling through an implant
Chain several hosts to reach a segmented target
Keep the chain stable when a single hop fails

chapters.title: Domain dominance and Active Directory abuse
objectives: Map the attack path to domain administrator and explain each hop
Abuse Active Directory Certificate Services to obtain usable credentials
Attack Kerberos authentication flaws such as delegation and ticket abuse
Use group policy and domain trusts to extend control
Show how domain control damages the whole organisation

chapters.title: Persistence and data hunting
objectives: Establish persistence so access survives a reboot or cleanup
Hunt for the data a real attacker would look for and rate its value
Exfiltrate data over a channel that blends with normal traffic
Explain why stealth matters more than speed at this stage
Note the evidence defenders should have seen and did not

chapters.title: Defence evasion
objectives: Explain how endpoint protection tools detect malicious behaviour
Evade common antivirus and script scanning controls during an operation
Work around application allowlisting without breaking the target
Adapt tooling when a defender blocks a technique mid operation
Recommend the defensive improvements that would have stopped you
